safe_word.how: Pick a word no one could guess from social media. Share it in person or by call, not in a group chat.

callback_rule.how: Agree: any money request by phone gets a hang-up and a call back on a saved number.

brief_relatives.how: A short call works best. Cover the safe word and the callback rule.

teen_controls.how: ChatGPT: Settings → Parental controls → Add family member (parents can't read chats). Snapchat: Family Center → Settings → Disable My AI. Gemini for under-13s: Family Link → child → Controls → Gemini. Character.AI ended open chat for under-18s in November 2025; Claude is 18+ only.

teen_talk.how: Ask what they use and what they like about it before any rules. Cover: it's built to keep them talking, it isn't a person, and they can come to you if a chat gets weird.

bank_voice_id_off.how: Call the number on your card. Say: "Please remove voice ID from my account and use a PIN or app approval instead."

phone.android: Phone app → Settings → Voicemail → Greeting (varies by carrier): pick the default.

voice_inventory.how: List every place your voice is public: videos, podcasts, talks, social posts, voice notes in public groups.

voice_audience.how: Go through the list and set each item to private, friends only, or delete it if it isn't needed.

youtube_likeness.how: In YouTube Studio, find likeness detection under content detection. It needs ID and a selfie.

likeness_monitoring.how: Create an account and add reference photos. It alerts you when your face shows up elsewhere.

face_search_optout.how: Submit the PimEyes opt-out form with a clear photo of your face. FaceCheck.ID has its own removal form. Results can reappear, so check again in a few months.

training_off_chatgpt.how: Settings → Data controls → Improve the model for everyone: off.

training_off_claude.how: Settings → Privacy → Help improve Claude: off.

activity_off_gemini.how: On the Gemini activity page, turn activity saving off. Delete past activity if you want.

training_off_copilot.how: Profile → Privacy → Model training on text: off. Also voice, if shown.

meta_ai_settings.how: In the Privacy Center, find AI at Meta. In the EU or UK, submit the objection form. Elsewhere, make posts you don't want used private.

training_off_linkedin.how: Settings → Data privacy → Data for Generative AI Improvement: off.

training_off_github.how: Settings → Copilot: turn off allowing GitHub to use your data for product improvements and training.

training_off_x.how: Settings → Privacy and safety → Data sharing and personalization → Grok & Third-party Collaborators: off. It's on by default.

assistant_memory.how: Open each assistant's memory or personalization settings. Delete anything you wouldn't want stored: health, money, other people.

push_back.how: In custom instructions or preferences, add: "Before you agree with me, give me the strongest case against my view." When it matters, ask as a question ("Is it true that…?") rather than stating your view. Instructions reduce agreement; they don't remove it.

agent_inventory.review: Run the check, then go through each tool with the user: what can it read, run, send or buy? Note anything they didn't know about.

agent_confirm.how: Keep approval prompts on for sending, paying and running commands. Avoid modes that skip all permission prompts.
agent_confirm.review: Run the check and point out any permissive mode or long allow list. Changing a tool's config file needs the user's OK on the exact change and a backup first.

agent_revoke.how: Remove connected tools and account connections that haven't been used in a month.
agent_revoke.review: Run the check and go through the connected tools by name. Remove only what the user picks; back up the config file first.

agent_banking.how: Use a separate browser profile for banking and never let an agent or AI browser work in it. Log out of email and bank before using an agent mode.

art_optout.how: DeviantArt and ArtStation now opt uploads out by default; check new uploads keep the NoAI setting. Adobe: turn off content analysis on the privacy page. Images on Meta follow the Meta step.

block_ai_crawlers.how: Builders: Squarespace and Wix have a setting; WordPress.com has "Prevent third-party sharing". Behind Cloudflare: turn on AI crawler blocking. Otherwise add the lines in the template to robots.txt. Training crawlers say they honour it; fetchers acting for a user often don't.

human_review_right.how: EU and UK: when a decision with real effects is made without a person, you can ask for a person to review it, give your side and get an explanation of how it was reached. California: similar rights for significant decisions from January 2027. Elsewhere, ask anyway.

ask_explanation.how: Write to the company's data protection or complaints contact: was software involved, which factors counted, which data it used, and how to get a person to review it. EU and UK companies must answer within a month.

fraud_reporting.how: Save the link as a bookmark, plus your bank's fraud phone number in your contacts.

deepfake_takedown.how: StopNCII makes a fingerprint of the image on your device so platforms can block it. The image itself isn't uploaded.

temporary_chat.how: ChatGPT: the Temporary button at the top of a new chat. Claude: the ghost icon at the top right (not inside projects). Neither feeds memory or training; both keep a copy for up to 30 days.

up_real_task.how: Pick something due this week, not a test question. Give it the material, ask for a first version, then push back two or three times until it's good.

up_context.how: In the personalization or profile settings, write a few lines: your role, what you work on, how you like answers (length, tone, what to skip).

think_first.how: Before asking about anything that matters, write two or three lines with your own answer. Then compare. It keeps the thinking yours.

work_rules.how: Find your employer's AI policy or ask IT which tools are approved. Use those for work files. Keep work documents out of personal accounts.

up_brief.how: Three parts: the goal and who it's for, the context it can't guess (files, constraints, past attempts), and what good looks like (length, format, an example).

up_project.how: Create a project, upload the files it should always know, and write the instructions once. Every chat inside it starts with that context.

verify_rule.how: Before anything goes out under your name: open every source, recheck every number, and confirm every quote and citation exists.

keep_skills.how: Pick the part of your work you'd want to still be good at in five years. Do it yourself now and then, and compare with what AI would have done.

up_connect.how: Start read-only with low stakes: a calendar or one folder. Check what the connection can do before you approve it.

up_schedule.how: Pick a task you already do every week (a summary, a digest, a check). Write the prompt once, set the schedule, and read the first few runs closely.

split_read_send.how: An agent that reads email or web pages shouldn't also be able to send, post or share on its own. Split it in two, or keep a confirm on every send.

review_schedule.how: Open the scheduled tasks page in each assistant. Delete what you no longer read and check what each one can reach.

vet_skills.how: Before installing a plugin, skill or connector, check who publishes it and what it can reach. Remove what you don't use.
vet_skills.review: Go through each plugin, skill and connected tool `check vet_skills` lists. For each: who makes it, what it can reach, still used? Suggest removing the rest; changes follow the config-file rule.

up_checks.how: Write the checklist you'd use yourself: what must be true before it's done. Tell the agent to check its work against it and report what failed.

up_workflow.how: Choose a workflow where a mistake is cheap to undo: drafts not sends, a test account, a copy of the files. Set limits first, then let it run end to end.

spend_limits.how: Give it a virtual card with a low limit, or no saved payment at all. Check your bank app for per-merchant limits.

action_log.how: Most agents keep a history of what they did. Once a week, skim it for anything you didn't expect.

undo_ready.how: Before it touches files, code or data: version history on, a backup, or a copy to work on. Agents have deleted real databases.
